It is the source of the largest and clearest known Iceland spar specimen and the source of most museum specimens of Iceland spar.
It was declared a nature reserve in 1975.


== About ==


=== Location ===

The mine is located near Eskifjörður, in the east of Iceland. Helgustaðir mine consists of two mines, known as the upper and lower mine.


=== Uses ===
Crystals from this area are known for exceptional clarity, leading to the mineral being named "Iceland spar".

Iceland spar from Helgustaðir mine was used in optical devices used in physics, chemistry, and geology, most importantly Nicol prisms.


=== Nature reserve ===
The nature reserve is 0.9 hectares. Since 2010, it has been on the Environment Agency of Iceland's red list of areas that are likely to lose their protection status.


== Theft of crystals ==
Being a nature reserve, tampering with the rock formations and removing crystals is forbidden. Despite that, visitors often take samples with them, causing a disruption of the area.
